significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that, across specified scientific mechanisms, intervention-induced output changes obey or violate independently measured laws in direction, monotonicity, and effect-size calibration, while many probe-decodable variables fail this test. This would establish both a phenomenon—a spectrum in the "fraction of mechanisms that pass"—and a causal mechanistic distinction that constrains whether probe-positive features can explain model predictions; this matters because work such as Vig et al.'s BERTology Meets Biology uses attention–biology associations, while the wider probing literature warns that decodability alone does not establish model use. The claim is reasonably determinate at the per-mechanism level, and a negative result in which probe-positive variables consistently produce law-calibrated effects would undermine the proposed correlate-versus-mechanism gap, although "many" and "approximate magnitude" leave the aggregate hypothesis somewhat loose. The topic-substitution check lowers this from the highest band: the law-calibrated intervention criterion and cross-mechanism fidelity spectrum, not merely the topic of scientific representations, support an above-median score.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "Mechanism Fidelity Score aggregating direction agreement, monotonicity, and effect-size calibration," intended as a model-auditing and model-selection diagnostic rather than merely an explanation. It can be ex ante when used to audit or select a model before relying on its scientific predictions, giving auditors and model users an action window, though scoring an individual failed prediction would be post hoc. After re-extraction on another model, the framework predicts the law-consistency relation to test but not that model's score or which mechanisms will pass; indeed, the claim says results are "model- and mechanism-specific," so primarily the audit procedure rather than the substantive finding transfers. The asserted scope spans protein, molecular, and small physics/materials models, and the topic-substitution check confirms that the score comes from the concrete fidelity metric and pre-deployment audit use—not from scientific foundation models being broadly important.
